questions.prompt: Okta issues SAML identity statements and Salesforce receives them for app sign-in. Which roles apply?

options.text: Okta is the IdP and Salesforce is the SP in this relationship
options.explanation: Provider roles depend on who issues and who relies on the statements.

options.text: The browser is the IdP because it carries the XML
options.explanation: Transport does not confer issuer authority.

options.text: Salesforce is always the IdP because it hosts business data
options.explanation: Hosting an app does not make it the statement issuer in this exchange.

options.text: Both systems must share one session cookie
options.explanation: Federation does not merge their local sessions.

review.heading: The application needs trustworthy identity information

questions.prompt: In a browser POST SAML response flow, who normally sends the form to the application's ACS?

options.text: The browser submits the provider-supplied form
options.explanation: The browser carries the response while the SP performs acceptance.

options.text: The IdP always sends the browser's POST directly server-to-server
options.explanation: That describes a different delivery path from the supplied browser form.

options.text: The local account record sends the request
options.explanation: An account record is not a network participant.

options.text: The ACS invents the provider's assertion
options.explanation: The IdP issues the assertion under its own trust relationship.

questions.prompt: What does an application's Assertion Consumer Service identify?

options.text: The receiving endpoint for the supported SAML response delivery
options.explanation: An ACS is a delivery location, distinct from the relying-party identifier.

options.text: The user's permanent employee number
options.explanation: A subject identifier is a different protocol role.

options.text: The required signing-key fingerprint
options.explanation: Key material does not name the receiving endpoint.

options.text: The final report page in every application
options.explanation: The post-login resource and protocol receiver need not be the same URL.

review.heading: The two sides need agreed configuration

questions.prompt: A production SP expects urn:app:prod, but an assertion permits only urn:app:test. What should happen?

options.text: The SP should reject the audience mismatch
options.explanation: Environment-specific relying-party targeting must fit the agreement.

options.text: Accept because both identifiers share a prefix
options.explanation: String resemblance does not make different audiences interchangeable.

options.text: Change the SP's identity based on incoming XML
options.explanation: Incoming data must not redefine the expected receiver.

options.text: Ignore targeting when the user has an account
options.explanation: Account existence does not cancel assertion restrictions.

questions.prompt: An assertion supplies a certificate and claims a familiar issuer. What must the receiver establish independently?

options.text: The expected provider and approved verification trust
options.explanation: A message cannot authorize its own signing material merely by supplying it.

options.text: Any embedded certificate is automatically trusted
options.explanation: An attacker can also supply certificate material.

options.text: The display name authenticates the key owner
options.explanation: Human-readable labels do not establish cryptographic trust.

options.text: The browser's successful delivery verifies the signer
options.explanation: Transport arrival is not signature verification.

questions.prompt: An SP expects employee ID E1042, but a trusted assertion contains an email NameID. What should be checked?

options.text: The emitted identity value and the agreed local account-matching rule
options.explanation: Trusted content can still disagree with the integration's identity contract.

options.text: Only the signature algorithm
options.explanation: Correct cryptography does not change the subject's value.

options.text: Only the response's Success status
options.explanation: Protocol success does not prove local account resolution.

options.text: Change the audience to the employee ID
options.explanation: Audience and subject identifier have different roles.

review.heading: A different NameID calls for a different investigation

evidence: SP account key: employee ID E1042
SP account resolution: no match under employee-ID rule

questions.prompt: An assertion's applicable validity limit has passed at the receiver. What is appropriate?

options.text: Enforce the time requirement using the controlled clock-tolerance policy
options.explanation: A valid signature does not remove applicable freshness restrictions.

options.text: Accept every signed assertion forever
options.explanation: Copies retain signatures and still need timing and replay controls.

options.text: Treat IssueInstant as an application session cookie
options.explanation: A message timestamp is not local session state.

options.text: Increase tolerance indefinitely until all attempts succeed
options.explanation: An unbounded allowance defeats the intended time restriction.

questions.prompt: An SP has pending request _r1, while a response's InResponseTo is _r2. What is the issue?

options.text: The response does not match the retained requested transaction
options.explanation: Correlation requires the actual acceptable pending context.

options.text: The user's display name needs changing
options.explanation: A display name does not identify the pending request.

options.text: A matching RelayState path automatically repairs it
options.explanation: Navigation context does not replace SAML correlation.

options.text: The ACS should rename its request to fit the response
options.explanation: Incoming data must not redefine the original pending transaction.

questions.prompt: A receiver verifies one assertion but consumes identity from an unsigned sibling. What must be fixed?

options.text: Bind identity consumption to the exact object whose required protection was verified
options.explanation: A nearby valid signature does not authenticate arbitrary sibling content.

options.text: Only check that both assertions have the same issuer text
options.explanation: Claimed origin is not authenticated coverage.

options.text: Base64-encode the entire document again
options.explanation: Encoding does not extend signature coverage.

options.text: Grant access if either object names the right audience
options.explanation: Target text does not authenticate the consumed identity.

questions.prompt: Okta records successful issuance, but no SP processing result is available. What remains unknown?

options.text: Whether the application accepted the response and created the intended session
options.explanation: Issuance is an upstream result rather than complete application access evidence.

options.text: Whether the provider reported issuance
options.explanation: That outcome is supplied directly.

options.text: Whether the app should evaluate incoming statements
options.explanation: The receiving SP retains that responsibility.

options.text: Whether assignment replaces account provisioning
options.explanation: Those responsibilities remain separate regardless of this missing result.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.

review.heading: The application needs trustworthy identity information

questions.prompt: The SP accepts SAML for an enabled reader but denies an administrative action. Which interpretation fits?

options.text: The application may be correctly enforcing local authorization
options.explanation: Federated sign-in does not grant every resource action.

options.text: Every administrative denial is a signature failure
options.explanation: The supplied acceptance succeeded before the resource check.

options.text: The IdP must promote the account to administrator
options.explanation: That would change permissions without the intended requirement.

options.text: The user must have no local account
options.explanation: An enabled reader account and session are already established.

review.heading: Authentication does not define the account lifecycle

questions.prompt: Local app logout ends the app session while an acceptable Okta session remains. What may happen on the next visit?

options.text: A new federation exchange can create a replacement app session without another prompt
options.explanation: Local termination and provider-session reuse are separate state changes.

options.text: The old app session necessarily survived
options.explanation: A new sign-in can explain the return without survival of old state.

options.text: Every other app must have logged out
options.explanation: No cross-app termination is established.

options.text: The same assertion must be replayed to regain entry
options.explanation: A new exchange can use fresh protocol messages.
